$comment: Pinned, SHA-verified FreeType SOURCE tarball for the M7 runtime-UI text substrate (src/packages/ui/text/, issue #237 / R-UI-005). SINGLE source of truth for the pin — read by cmake/ContextFreetype.cmake (string(JSON)) which fetches + verifies (cmake/ContextDownload.cmake) + extracts + add_subdirectory's FreeType's own first-class CMake to build the `freetype` target. Unlike the MSVC/Clang-ABI prebuilts (V8/wgpu-native/CEF/wasmtime — fetched as opaque binaries), FreeType is portable C built FROM SOURCE here (the WAMR-from-pinned-source precedent), so it compiles under the local Strawberry-GCC dev gate AND all three CI build legs with no prebuilt. LICENSE ELECTION: FreeType is dual-licensed 'FTL OR GPL-2.0-or-later' (docs/FTL.TXT / docs/GPLv2.TXT) — we ELECT the FreeType License (FTL), NEVER the GPL limb (DECISION-a7a8-deps.md, owner-delegated Fable verdict = GO). The build DISABLES every optional subsystem (FT_DISABLE_ZLIB/BZIP2/PNG/HARFBUZZ/BROTLI): embedded raw TTFs need none, and disabling HarfBuzz severs the FreeType<->HarfBuzz circular option + minimizes the attack surface (R-SEC-006). The official release tarball (make-dist, byte-stable — NOT a regenerated git-archive) is fetched from the FreeType home on savannah; the pin below is that artifact's SHA-256. Upstream LICENSE.TXT/FTL.TXT/GPLv2.TXT are vendored verbatim under third_party/freetype/ (NOTICE flow-down); tools/license-allowlist.json records 'freetype':'FTL'.
$comment_mirrors: AVAILABILITY (issue #359): this fetch runs at CONFIGURE time inside the DEFAULT build (src/packages/ui/text/ sits in nearly every leg's dependency closure), so ONE host being down reds the ENTIRE CI rollup — measured 2026-07-22, when download.savannah.gnu.org returned 502 for ~an hour and failed 7 unrelated jobs across all three OSes. `url` stays the upstream home and is tried FIRST; `mirrors` are ordered fallbacks tried only after it is exhausted. SECURITY IS UNCHANGED: every source is verified against the SAME `sha256` below, so a mirror serving different bytes is REFUSED and skipped, and the fetch still fails CLOSED when no source yields the pinned artifact (R-SEC-009). ADDING A MIRROR: fetch the candidate and confirm its SHA-256 equals `sha256` byte-for-byte BEFORE listing it — an unverified mirror is not a mirror. Prefer INDEPENDENT infrastructure: `download.savannah.gnu.org` is itself a redirect DISPATCHER onto downstream mirrors, so a second savannah.gnu.org hostname is only partial redundancy, while SourceForge is a genuinely uncorrelated host and is therefore listed first. All three below were verified byte-identical (4063324 bytes) on 2026-07-25. On a VERSION BUMP every mirror URL must be re-pointed at the new version and re-verified — tools/check_source_pins.py enforces that each mirror URL carries the pinned `version`, so a forgotten mirror fails python-tests instead of quietly pointing at the previous tarball. That gate is OFFLINE and STRUCTURAL, though: a mirror that is well-formed but has since been REMOVED upstream (a retired project path) passes it forever and would only surface during the outage it exists for. So the byte-identical verification above is the author's duty at listing time and must be redone on every bump — the gate catches a forgotten mirror, not a dead one.
